name: icon
why: Icon is a goal-directed language with generators and backtracking, a genuinely different way of thinking about control flow from the Arizona lineage.

brief.what_it_is: Icon is a high-level, general-purpose programming language. The homepage highlights two features: string scanning and goal-directed evaluation. The page offers source downloads for Unix (including Linux, Macintosh, and Cygwin) and a separate download for Microsoft Windows. The homepage does not describe inputs or outputs in detail, and it shows no example program.
brief.why_it_exists: Icon was first released in 1979 as a modern successor to SNOBOL4, and it continued to evolve for the next two decades.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage names goal-directed evaluation and string scanning as the core novel features but does not explain the mechanism. The scout notes describe generators and backtracking, but the homepage does not confirm those details.
brief.install_notes: The homepage links to a Unix download (Linux, Macintosh, Cygwin) and a separate Windows download. It gives no build steps, runtime requirements, or first-run instructions. The brew metadata lists three executables: icon, icont, and iconx. I did not see those names on the homepage. The homepage links to Getting Started, Current Documentation, and a Language Reference, but I did not have their URLs and did not fetch them.
brief.standout: Goal-directed evaluation, where expressions can produce multiple results and the runtime backtracks to find one that succeeds, is a different control-flow model from most mainstream languages. The homepage presents it as a central feature of the language.
brief.status: Maintenance mode. The homepage says development has been frozen, but the Unix implementation is still in active use and is maintained as necessary. I saw no release date or commit date on the page.
brief.caveats: The homepage says development is frozen, so no new language features are expected. The Windows build is a separate download and I did not check its state. The homepage does not say whether the language is licensed for commercial use. I did not read the README, docs, or release notes, so I have no command examples and no installation details beyond the download links.
quotes: Icon is a high-level, general-purpose programming language with novel features including string scanning and goal-directed evaluation.
Development has now been frozen, but the Unix implementation is still in active use and is maintained as necessary.
Icon was first released in 1979 as a modern successor to SNOBOL4, and it continued to evolve for the next two decades.
fetch_log: https://www2.cs.arizona.edu/icon/ - fetched OK, returned the project homepage text (not a GitHub repo, so no README). Sub-page links on the page have no URLs in the fetched text, so I did not follow any further links.
